majors.finding: The label was the registration wizard's own button. RegistrationFlow.tsx:260 is `label="Add another child"` word for word, and SiblingScreen.tsx:178 wears the identical brand-600/15 + ring brand-500/40 + brand-300 costume for its *registration* offer. A parent who pressed a blue tinted ringed pill saying 'Add another child' and landed on a keyboard would press the one blue tinted ringed pill on the new screen — creating a duplicate student record for a child already on the roster. The evening's attendance lands on the duplicate and Tuesday's MIA list phones a family whose child was in the room.
majors.note: SiblingScreen's own header records that '+ Add a brother or sister' was removed from this screen for exactly this reason. r1 collapsed both distinctions keeping them apart — grey text vs blue pill, and 'Find' vs 'Add' — in one move. The critic retracted its own round-1 recommendation.
majors.fixed_by: The label lost its verb: '+ Another child ›'. A noun phrase cannot collide with 'Add' or fight 'Find'. Fill to brand-600/32 so the two pills are not the same costume either.

majors.finding: r1 flattened the region and deleted the min-h-0 overflow-y-auto the real component carries — whose own comment says it 'is what lets it shrink instead of pushing the button off a short screen'. At five siblings on the landscape kiosk the student's *name* goes off the top of the glass and Back off the bottom. MAX_FAMILY_OFFER is 7, so eight children is supported. Landscape-only, which is why an N=1 frame hid it.
majors.fixed_by: Sibling rows are a scroller again; the add-row hangs below it, inside the region, so the names scroll and the way to add one never does. New `many` scene at five siblings.

design_minors_acted_on: 40px identity→region was set box-to-box and rendered 43–49 once line-box slack was paid, leaving the region equidistant between name and commit and 'another' without a visible antecedent. Now 32px of ink; column ramps 14/32/48/76.
The add-row's fill (1.14:1) was fainter than the ink-800 sibling row beside it (1.38:1) — a recipe tuned for a pill a sixth the area, so the box existed on its 1px ring alone. Now brand-600/32.

The row's right half was 182px of empty tint, which in the list's own grammar reads as an *unticked* sibling. Now a chevron at the right inset — and a chevron is not a state chip, which the tick column is for.
Five type sizes, three of them one voice. The ask joined Back at 20px.

The plus could not hold a left edge inline (13px light glyph against a 20px semibold cap). The region gained a 48px leading gutter instead, shared by the ask and the sibling rows, so every line starts on one x.
still_open: The identity is centred, so the name and commit each move 56px between scenes and there is no fixed spine in either axis. Design wants it anchored; usability praised the compact centred band as reachable. Deliberately not done — carried to round 3 with four scenes to measure against.
The wide frame is still the tall frame's composition in a landscape hole: 416px of empty page each side, 65% of the width.
SearchScreen runs a 672px column; this screen runs 448px, with byte-identical row markup.
fidelity_gaps_closed: The commit hardcoded 'Check in'; the real component says 'Check in all N' whenever a sibling is ticked, and that count is the only place on the screen reporting how many children the tap covers.
Neither round had shot the outcome the change exists to produce. New `added` scene: the parent came back from the sibling screen with the missed child, ticked.
implementation_note: ConfirmScreen.tsx gates this affordance on intent !== 'check-out'. The prototype's region is unconditional; a collection screen must not grow an 'Another child' row above a blue 'Hold to collect'.
